title: Tuck channel header actions into hover controls
summary: The root ask was delivered in commit 578e160, which is present in current main history. Channel headers show the name at rest; description, archive/settings (including Task filter), and copy-link actions are tucked into hover/focus controls on desktop and remain touch-accessible on phones. Product Development Lead reported desktop/phone screenshot review, client invariant checks, typecheck, and mobile channel tests. A related archive project remains in review for isolated mobile archive/restore integration and live verification; that separate gap does not reopen the header request.
nextAction: Archive project owner/Product Development Lead to coordinate with Release Engineer to integrate mobile commit 53ebe1c after concurrent ChannelsMobile.tsx edits are committed, then live-verify archive/restore on phone and desktop after a safe server reload.
evidence: Root post post_01a0e226-04ed-754d-a66b-d9a8f4dd505d asks to move Archive into a hover-revealed gear, move description into a hover-revealed info icon, and remove the All posts and link controls from the resting header.
Thread reply post_01a0e230-00ab-7073-89fb-6fd32d1919f7 by Product Development Lead reports completion in 578e160 and screenshot, client invariant, typecheck, and mobile channel test checks.

Commit 578e160 ('Tuck channel header actions into hover controls') changes ChannelArchive.tsx, ChannelBrowser.tsx/CSS, ChannelHeaderControls.css, ChannelsMobile.tsx, mobile channel CSS, and mobile channel tests. Commit is reachable from current main HEAD b39dca3.

Current task buddy_project_df417ed0-dc56-4287-b53d-59cd7fa75174 is in review. Its acceptance criteria cover archive/restore policy, hidden archived channels, recoverable posts, UI actions, and integration tests. Task evidence records package/server/desktop work and screenshots; nextAction explicitly calls out isolated mobile UI commit 53ebe1c plus live phone/desktop verification.
limitations: This is a read-only review; reported checks/screenshots were not rerun.
Workspace has extensive unrelated dirty files; commit contents and reachability were used as evidence, not the dirty working tree.
No direct UI inspection or live archive/restore verification was performed.
